description: Vamos trabalhar Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data
summary:
EARTH+ BR is a responsive website developed to democratize access to technology and Earth observation data for family farmers and small- and medium-sized agricultural producers.
The platform addresses this challenge by transforming complex NASA scientific information into a clear, user-friendly tool that is easy to adopt and highly accessible in rural areas. Through an interactive map, an intelligent chatbot for direct inquiries, and automatically generated downloadable reports, farmers can instantly analyze soil moisture and precipitation using official data from NASA SMAP, GPM, MODIS, and NASA POWER, as well as simulate different scenarios through a Crop Rotation Comparator.
Our key impact advantage: While traditional analyses can take days to process using complex software, EARTH+ BR delivers answers in seconds. Projections based on precision agriculture models indicate that the preventive use of the platform could lead to an estimated reduction of up to 25% in water waste for irrigation, combining strong environmental sustainability with a direct increase in farmers' profitability.
EARTH+ BR turns NASA's orbital science into real-world prosperity and climate resilience on the ground.
details:
Project Overview & Operational Mechanism: EARTH+ BR is a responsive web application engineered to empower smallholder family farmers in Northeast Brazil to adapt agricultural practices to climate variability through NASA’s Earth observation data. Utilizing an intuitive interactive mapping interface, producers delineate their property boundaries—either via point selection or polygon drawing—and immediately receive accessible, plain-language diagnostics comparing current precipitation, soil moisture, and temperature metrics against the 2001–2020 historical baseline. Furthermore, the platform delivers a dynamic Land Calendar, crop suitability and rotation recommendations, an AI-driven conversational assistant (operating via text or voice grounded in the property’s real-time geospatial data), and automated, downloadable PDF reports for offline field reference.

Technical Architecture, Stack & Data Integration: Our backend queries NASA POWER for localized agro-climatic historical series and cross-references NASA GPM IMERG satellite precipitation datasets, NASA SMAP root-zone soil moisture, MODIS vegetation health indices (NDVI), and FAO GAEZ v4 crop suitability models—retrieved programmatically via NASA Harmony and the Common Metadata Repository (CMR). Configurable agronomic rule engines transform these complex scientific datasets into actionable indicators, comparative analyses, and structured reports.

  • Backend & Geospatial Engine: Python, FastAPI, pandas, xarray, shapely, SQLite, and ReportLab.
  • Frontend & Cartographic Interface: Responsive web architecture built with React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Leaflet integrated with high-resolution satellite imagery.

Value Proposition, Benefits & Intended Impact: Whereas conventional analysis of raw orbital datasets demands days of specialized GIS processing, EARTH+ BR delivers actionable agronomic intelligence within seconds—guiding underserved farmers without access to continuous technical assistance on optimal crop selection, planting windows, and soil conservation. Precision agriculture benchmarks documented by NASA Harvest and the FAO (Global Agro-Ecological Zones & Precision Agriculture reports) indicate that preventive management guided by orbital soil moisture and precipitation data can yield an estimated reduction of up to 25% in irrigation water waste alongside a 15% improvement in soil nutrient retention, mitigating crop losses caused by drought and irregular rainfall while directly enhancing smallholder profitability and climate resilience.

Innovation & Human-Centered Design Considerations: To bridge the technical divide in rural communities, we engineered a rapid, 10-question visual onboarding assessment supported by photographic references, paired with a text-and-voice assistant anchored to each farm’s exact geographic coordinates. Every architectural choice prioritized mobile-first usability, accessible terminology, offline operational resilience via local data caching for unstable rural connectivity, and complete scientific transparency regarding the origin of every metric presented.
